Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}+{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-[\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\frac{\pi }{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})] \\  & +[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})] \\  & =[\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 0-\frac{\pi }{6}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}]+[1-\frac{1}{2}] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\pi }{12}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
